title: Learning-technology adoption radar
goal: A school district can distinguish mature high-value tools from emerging experiments.

rubric.must: Named technologies are visibly positioned by maturity and instructional value.
The mature high-value learning-management system is visibly distinct from emerging tools.
Bubble sizes visibly encode relative scale.
Both axes are labelled and directional.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the matrix/quadrant exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: All four technologies are visibly placed in the maturity–instructional-value matrix. The learning management system is distinct in the mature, high-value quadrant; bubble sizes vary, both axes are labelled with clear directional arrows, and all technology labels are readable without material overlap or cropping.

items.evidence: AI feedback assistant and virtual reality lab are on the emerging side; learning management system and classroom clickers are on the mature side. Their vertical positions distinguish higher from lower instructional value.
The learning management system is visibly in the mature, high-value quadrant, separate from both emerging tools.
Bubble areas visibly vary across the technologies, with the learning management system largest and the virtual reality lab smallest, matching their relative scale values.
The horizontal axis is labelled Maturity and points toward Mature; the vertical axis is labelled Instructional Value and points toward High instructional value.
All four technology names and their scale values are readable and do not materially overlap bubbles or quadrant boundaries.
